V, 9ᵇ</cite> <he>א׳ שהיא מריוח</he> the reference to rain (in the second section of the eighteen benedictions) which is an expression of satisfaction (plenty), opp. <cite ref="U00033"><he>שאלה</he></cite>, the prayer for rain (in the ninth benediction) which is an expression of anxiety.—
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 3:4:3">Y. Meg. III, 74ᵇ</cite> top <he>שתהא אַזְכָּרָתָן קודם וכ׳</he> that the recitation (of the events commemorated on Purim) precede the celebration thereof.

<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 2:1">Num. R. s. 2</cite>, beg. the students <he>מראים את הא׳ וכ׳</he> point out the Div. Name with their fingers; <cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 2:4:1">Cant. R. to II, 4</cite> <he>מדלג על הא׳</he> skips the Div. Name in recitation of lessons.—Pl. <he>אַזְכָּרוֹת</he>.
<cite ref="Yoma 8a:1">Yoma 8ᵃ</cite> <he>שיש בהן א׳ הרבה</he> in which the Div. N. frequently occurs.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 3:4:12">Y. Ber. III, 6ᶜ</cite>.—Y. Sabb. XVI, 15ᶜ bot.; Bab.
<cite ref="Shabbat 116a:8">ibid. 116ᵃ</cite> <he>קודר אזכרותֵיהֶן</he> you must cut out the Div. N. occurring in them (the heretic writings).
Y. Taan. II, 65ᶜ top י״ח א׳ וכ׳ eighteen times that the Tetragrammaton appears in the Psalm Habu (XXIX).
